hypothesis: Adding deterministic opaque cursors bound to the reviewed snapshot and exact filters will let hosts retrieve every provenance record without duplicates or cross-filter reuse now that the feed exceeds its 20-record response limit, while preserving the companion's offline read-only boundary.
heldOutChecks: the first limited page returns a next cursor, total matches and the newest records in stable order
following the cursor returns the exact next records without overlap or gaps
project and kind filters remain applied across every continued page
tampered, stale-snapshot and cross-filter cursors fail closed
CLI continuation matches library pagination and invalid cursors exit nonzero
MCP exposes the cursor schema, preserves read-only annotations, returns the same continued page and rejects invalid cursors

memoryDecision.ruvectorWasm: defer until at least 100 sanitized provenance records support leakage-free exact, vector and fused retrieval comparisons
memoryDecision.gnn: reject for the current corpus unless a held-out graph task demonstrates at least ten percentage points of task-success gain over exact filtering and a shuffled-graph control

forecast.prediction: Within 90 days, agent registries and provenance ledgers will increasingly bind opaque continuation cursors to a snapshot or query identity rather than expose reusable offsets.
forecast.falsifiableCriterion: By 2026-12-15, at least two primary agent-memory, MCP, or tool-registry implementations newly publish snapshot-, revision-, or query-bound cursor invalidation semantics for provenance retrieval.
